dedupe_keys.name: gcat general catalog of artificial space objects jonathan mcdowell

description: GCAT, the General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects, makes public the full satellite database behind Jonathan McDowell's Jonathan's Space Report, covering every artificial object outside Earth's lower atmosphere: active payloads, rocket stages, discarded components and debris. Its data model tracks each object through phases of flight, attachment, surface presence and destruction. Coverage: global and historical; release 1.8.8 of 3 September 2026 with a data update on 28 September 2026 includes the main satellite catalogue (satcat), auxiliary, failed-to-orbit and extended catalogues (including Space Force analyst objects and numbers above 100000), temporary and complementary lists, suborbital and low catalogues, event, deep space, heliocentric and lunar and planetary registers, payload catalogues, organisations, launch sites and launch points, launch platforms, launch vehicles and full launch lists, plus derived current, geosynchronous and active catalogues and an orbital launch log. Format and access: fixed-width text and TSV tables per catalogue, tar.gz bundles of all catalogues, and PDF documentation of definitions, conventions and column meanings; free and without registration. Licence: CC-BY-4.0, with a requested short citation 'data from GCAT (J. McDowell, planet4589.org/space/gcat)'. Caveats: the catalogue is maintained by one researcher; fixed-width files truncate column names; some objects carry vague dates recorded in a documented uncertain-date format. Simulation uses: satellite population, orbit class and ownership data for modelling satellite communications and positioning dependencies, debris cascades and space weather exposure. Related records: CelesTrak element sets and SATCAT (data-celestrak-gp-satcat) give current orbits, and the same author's constellation list (data-mcdowell-mega-constellations-list) tracks large constellations.
